target.name: cjson
target.description: cJSON, a widely used C JSON parser. The base revision contains a heap buffer over-read in parse_object(): after consuming the comma between object members it reads the next byte without checking that the byte is inside the supplied length.

base.subject: Add test for heap buffer overflow
base.author: orri <orri@systemb.is>

hunks.header: @@ -1660,6 +1660,11 @@ static cJSON_bool parse_object(cJSON * const item, parse_buffer * const input_bu
hunks.context: static cJSON_bool parse_object(cJSON * const item, parse_buffer * const input_bu

tests.note: 100 levels, well inside cJSON's documented nesting limit of 1000.
cJSON_ParseWithLength parses a value from the start of the buffer and does not require the buffer to be consumed. See SPECIFICATION.md 4.2.
Same defect reached with a different key and value length.
The same shape one level deeper, reached through a nested object.

Control case. The array path was already correct upstream, so this input should be rejected cleanly by both versions. Its presence shows the object-path finding is a specific defect, not an artefact of truncation.

oracle.semantics: An object that ends immediately after a member separator is incomplete and must be rejected without reading past the supplied length.

limitations: a position-independent executable does not establish that ASLR is active at run time; that is a property of the kernel and the execution environment, not of the binary
evidence of a stack canary shows the protection is in use somewhere, not that every function is protected; the compiler decides per function
the absence of a mitigation here is a property of this build only, and says nothing about how the project is built elsewhere
